correctness.rationale: All 1-to-5-run cases are partitioned into attainable run patterns. In the five-run case, even-run outputs extend, the five-run optimum has symmetric caps, and the four two-sided embeddings of 0-1-0 outputs yield either strict domination by a longer palindrome or symmetric maximum caps. The two other three-run patterns also have symmetric maximum caps. Four-run and fewer inputs receive independent exhaustive pattern cases. The six one-doubled-run words starting with zero give all length-seven sharpness configurations, modulo complement. Reproducibility program completed independent brute subsequence enumeration for 1,022 inputs through length nine and full LCS recurrence enumeration for 8,190 words through length twelve and 1,024 positive five-run tuples. The proof rather than those enumerations handles arbitrary positive run lengths.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Equal optimum lengths and existence of one palindrome are strictly weaker than every maximum output being a palindrome. Deterministic safe backtracking also selects only some optimum paths and cannot imply universal safety on a particular input class. The present quantified condition is thus not a corollary of those results.

originality.rationale: The ESA 2024 primary paper demonstrates that some LCS outputs of a string and its reversal fail palindromicity and proves that specific backtracking choices avoid failure. It does not state the binary at-most-five-run all-optima criterion, the six-run sharp boundary, or the unique shortest obstruction orbit. The 2011 LCPS study solves a different problem where palindromicity is imposed. Actual semantic record and web-query comparisons found no equivalent structural theorem; remaining unindexed sources are an explicit risk.

value.rationale: The all-optima versus existence distinction is directly motivated by the 2024 reversal-LCS reconstruction problem. The result gives an input-structural and algorithm-independent guarantee for every binary word with up to five arbitrarily long constant runs; six runs are proven necessary for failure, with the earliest four input words completely classified. The exact run threshold is a meaningful boundary for when arbitrary LCS reconstruction is palindromic, not a mere restatement of classical LCS/LPS length equality or an arbitrary isolated count.
